profile: regulated platform; bounded development-only local HQ capability
partitionSemantics: Disjoint Node test-name-pattern selections omit nonselected groups in each invocation; every one of the28 source groups executed exactly once across final partitions. Omitted groups are not counted as passes or skips.

partitions.namePattern: restricted bootstrap|legacy adoption|wrong, unknown|cancelled recovery|confirmed response|audit persistence|revoked retained|HTTP recovery|unauthenticated challenges|invalid proof budget|request queued|adopted second-seat|expired saved-factor|lost signout
groups: security: restricted bootstrap cannot read domain data, create sessions or nominate another seat
security: legacy adoption requires the original valid seat proof and preserves both workspaces
security: wrong, unknown and cross-instance recovery factors cannot guess or change a seat
security: cancelled recovery and rotation retain the current factor until confirmed commit
security: confirmed response loss is resolved by redacted receipt and saved replacement, never another cookie
security: audit persistence failure rolls back factor, generation, revocation and receipt atomically
security: revoked retained request objects and stale CSRF cannot read or commit commands
security: HTTP recovery challenge is bound to the exact browser while bad origin, body and forged scope refuse
security: unauthenticated challenges cannot replace a proved pending seat operation or disable normal sessions
security: invalid proof budget persists across reopen and never disables an existing valid session
security: a request queued after initial authorization rechecks its seat inside the write transaction
security: adopted second-seat enrollment requires exact current cookie and one-use local permit together
security: expired saved-factor stage consumes only the stage and leaves old factor and session usable
security: lost signout or revoke responses replay receipts without clearing or revoking a newer session

partitions.namePattern: guarded open refuses|cached guard loss|native Windows junction|native owner custody|replaced database|inert markers|guard loss after|explicit insecure|actual running|same-inode
groups: security: guarded open refuses missing database, guard, both and parent without implicit creation
security: cached guard loss blocks reads and writes while preserving existing business rows
security: native Windows junction and hard-linked database aliases refuse without rebinding
security: native owner custody rejects an insecure instance directory
security: replaced database and swapped guard cannot be adopted as the cached authoritative instance
security: inert markers, moved inert application identity and unenrolled legacy storage refuse normal guarded open
security: guard loss after a real business write rolls back before commit and closes the cached handle
security: explicit insecure guard and database file ACLs refuse even under an owner-only directory
security: actual running Windows database rename either denies replacement or closes the orphaned cached handle
security: same-inode native overwrite is detected instead of serving stale cached SQLite pages

partitions.namePattern: encrypted new-schema|old v1 fixture|truly concurrent|early partial
groups: security: encrypted new-schema capture physically excludes every auth control and restores inert with exact business history
security: old v1 fixture package remains fully inspectable and inert after access schema support
security: truly concurrent worker confirmations produce one session and one committed transition
security: early partial initialization and adoption stay blocked until exact owned-operation resume with original proof

sourceReview: Independent reread of access protocol, native storage custody, exact identity, cached and fresh metadata guards, HTTP boundary, bootstrap and two-seat proof authorization, transactional generation/session/audit, replay material, bounded diagnostics, source-only backup rebuild and ciphertext/raw-page exclusion.

Independent reread of frozen UI/client/fields/dialog/provider/shell, canonical15-agent return allowlist, unknown outcome handling, separate fixture launcher and unchanged legacy launcher. Actual browser QA is separate independent QA evidence.
ESLint one-line generated fixture output ignore matches existing generated Next output ignores; lint rules unchanged.
Operations guide correctly limits all helpers and launcher to marked external synthetic fixtures, separates cookies/browser profile and holds real/live/production/activation/external finance actions.
authorizationBoundary: A current same-seat cookie authorizes its permitted HQ reads/writes and signout only; recovery/enrollment/rotation/revoke-all require their additional exact factor or local permit and proofs. Restricted bootstrap grants no ordinary HQ access. No business roles or cross-seat authority.
priorEvidence: Original RED failures, interrupted obsolete execution, refusal-label and missing-operation-material harness corrections, and pre-audit-label candidate28 receipts retained; they are not final acceptance receipts.
releaseLimits: No real data, .local-volabi, real cookies, real recovery/enrollment, launcher replacement, production, business activation, Azure or financial/external action.
Global regulated release gates are owned by root and are not waived by this capability acceptance.
development-credential-diagnostic-exposure remains HIGH/open; no credential values copied.
Dependency/runtime advisories require separate applicability and maintenance follow-up; no whole-platform security-clear claim.
independence: No product implementation edits, no other test edits, no self-review, no commit or push by this reviewer.
